instruction: For each course wave represented by at least one fully observed ticket, report the smallest and largest possible counts of late tickets. Each row describes one distinct ticket. Its kitchen acceptance and pass handoff occurred at unknown integer minutes in the respective inclusive first/last ranges, measured from the same service opening. Every combination of endpoints within a complete row is feasible, and tickets can vary independently. A ticket is late only if handoff minus acceptance strictly exceeds its own allowance in minutes. Equality is on time. A NULL handoff_last means observation stopped before an upper bound was recorded. Exclude that ticket from both counts and the denominator. All other fields are non-NULL. Return wave_code, observed_tickets, min_late, max_late, ordered by wave_code ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Each batch has one missing integer horizontal fold offset in pixels. The scanner applies it by adding it to raw_x. On each calibration strip the corrected coordinate must lie within the inclusive interval from band_lo to band_hi. A NULL endpoint means only that side of the interval is unbounded. Use all strips for each batch appearing in fold_strip. Return ordered columns batch_code, finding, offset_px sorted by batch_code ascending. Use finding 'conflict' if no integer satisfies the strips, 'resolved' if exactly one does, and 'open' if several do. Return the integer only for 'resolved', otherwise NULL. Equal endpoints are admissible and duplicate bounds carry no extra weight. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

For the Aster release erratum about blank page previews, report each printer profile with a verified fix boundary. Each bench_slip is primary evidence from one preview test. Build numbers are integer release-build ordinals shared by all profiles. A boundary requires a blank preview on one build and a visible preview on the immediately following numbered build for the same profile. A missing build supplies no evidence. If a profile qualifies repeatedly, use the latest qualifying boundary. Each profile/build pair is unique, slip IDs are unique, and no values are null. Return profile_code, fixed_build, blank_slip, visible_slip in ascending binary profile_code order. Both citations must identify the slips that establish the reported boundary. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: For each dryer meter, find the tightest observation-supported time interval containing its one counter reset during the shift. Signed field slips record the display's reset lamp as OLD before the reset or NEW from the instant of reset onward. Unsigned slips are unverified. The structured lamp_code transcribes the lamp named in the primary text. Use signed slips only and include a meter only when both lamp states were witnessed. Return meter_code, after_min, by_min, old_source, new_source ordered by meter_code ascending. Times are whole minutes after shift start, with the lower endpoint exclusive and the upper endpoint inclusive. Cite the actual slip ID supporting each endpoint. At equal times for the same endpoint choose the lexicographically smallest supporting slip ID. Slip IDs are unique, signed observations are consistent, and no input fields are null. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.
